stem: The value of ∫ from 0 to π/2 of log(sin x) dx is
explanation: Correct option: (C). Let I be the integral. By P4, I = ∫ from 0 to π/2 of log(cos x) dx. Adding, 2I = ∫ log(sin x cos x) dx = ∫ log(sin 2x) dx − (π/2) log 2. With t = 2x and P6, ∫ from 0 to π/2 of log(sin 2x) dx = I. So 2I = I − (π/2) log 2, giving I = −(π/2) log 2. The positive value has the wrong sign (log sin x ≤ 0 on the interval); −π log 2 is 2I, not I; −(π/4) log 2 halves the result once too often.
